newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end firmer, boosted by bonds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end firmer, boosted by bonds.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

CANDLR 1.3499 LME CASH ALUM US$1591 -7.0
CAN 30-YR 111.65 +1.05 MAR BRENT CRUDE US$21.02 -0.74
* Toronto stocks closed firmer after an active session, powered by a rally in bonds and strength in heavily weighted banking group. * Golds turned positive following weak start.
Toronto stocks closed on a firmer note on Friday, boosted by a party in the bond market and strength in the heavily weighted banking and gold sectors.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 29.85 points to reach 6101.74, with 111 million shares traded worth C$1.74 billion.

North American markets surged after the release of the U.S. January jobless rate. It edged up to 5.4 percent from 5.3, providing indications that the job market has not tightened enough for employers to bid up wages and that the Federal Reserve may not raise interest rates.
Bonds rallied dropping yields, so Canadian investors fled to the high-yielding Toronto stock market.
"It's acting on any piece of news," said Montreal-based strategist Bill Ram.
Advances inched ahead of declines 507 to 490 while another 276 traded flat.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, banks rose the most, adding two percent to hit new highs. Other strong groups were consumer products, golds and base metals.
The weaker side included conglomerates, oils and pipelines, which kept Toronto from jumping as high as Wall Street.
Over the course of the week Toronto's stock exchange retraced its steps from a new lifetime high of 6159.18 points on Wednesday to today's close.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Cara Operations Ltd class A rose 0.05 to 4.15 on three million shares after announcing positive third quarter results yesterday.

* Viceroy Homes Ltd shares lost more than half their value, falling 5.40 to 5.00 after reporting lower than forecast fourth quarter earnings today. Net income for the quarter plunged 61 percent to C$409,000.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100))
